answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with adaptive identity pricing: each new identity pays a verification cost that rises with the tide of fresh registrations, so a flood of fake accounts gets expensive fast while one genuine agent barely notices. The price tracks the live pulse of the network — registration rate and attestation density — and is set by a reef of long-established identities whose own stake is slashed if they approve fakes. An attacker funding thousands of identities must pay the escalating price on every one, while honest agents join cheaply during quiet periods.
